def: Located above the vocal cords (glottis), in the region of the epiglottis and false cords. Supraglottic collapse causes airway obstruction in laryngomalacia, and supraglottic swelling in epiglottitis.
Relating to the periosteum, the connective tissue sheath covering the outer surface of bone. Periosteal bone growth thickens bone, as in acromegaly.
The thyroid step in which thyroid peroxidase attaches oxidized iodine to tyrosine residues of thyroglobulin, forming MIT and DIT. Blocked by thioamide drugs.
1,25-dihydroxycholecalciferol, also called calcitriol, the active form of vitamin D. Made in the kidney by 1-alpha-hydroxylase, it raises calcium and phosphate absorption in the gut.
An injectable analog of amylin that slows gastric emptying and suppresses glucagon, used with mealtime insulin in diabetes. Can cause hypoglycemia and nausea.
The border on the cervix where squamous epithelium of the ectocervix meets columnar epithelium of the endocervix. The transformation zone here is where HPV-related dysplasia arises.
Twin pregnancy in which both fetuses share a single amniotic sac, with a risk of umbilical cord entanglement. Arises when the embryo splits at days 8 to 12.
Failure of chromosomes or sister chromatids to separate properly during meiosis or mitosis, causing aneuploidy such as trisomy 21 or Turner syndrome.
Having a warty, rough surface. Libman-Sacks endocarditis involves verrucous vegetations on both sides of the mitral valve in lupus.
Attached by a stalk (peduncle), as in a polyp or a cardiac myxoma that hangs in the left atrium.
A shift of a cell's membrane potential to a more negative value, making it less likely to fire. Adenosine causes it in the SA and AV nodes by opening potassium channels.
A higher concentration of red cells in the blood from loss of plasma volume, as in dehydration, or from chronic hypoxia that raises erythropoiesis.
Describes necrosis with a soft, cheese-like, structureless appearance, typical of tuberculosis granulomas.
Describes granulomas with no central necrosis, seen in sarcoidosis, Crohn disease and berylliosis.
Abnormally hard tissue from swelling or fibrosis. A positive tuberculin skin test is judged by the width of induration.
Resembling epithelial cells. Epithelioid macrophages, activated and plump with pink cytoplasm, form granulomas.
The rising osmolarity from the renal cortex to the papillary tip, built by the loop of Henle and urea, which lets the collecting duct concentrate urine under ADH.
Beneath the periosteum, the sheath covering bone. Subperiosteal bone resorption is a classic sign of hyperparathyroidism.
Spread of cancer or infection through the bloodstream. Renal cell carcinoma spreads this way after invading the renal vein.
Crossing of nerve fibers from one side of the central nervous system to the other, such as the corticospinal tracts at the medullary pyramids.
A medullary nucleus receiving upper body fine-touch and proprioception fibers of the dorsal column (fasciculus cuneatus). Its second-order neurons cross to form the medial lemniscus.
Abnormally thick blood, from excess red cells or paraproteins, causing headache, visual changes and bleeding. Seen in polycythemia vera and Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia.
Small penetrating branches of the middle cerebral artery supplying the basal ganglia and internal capsule. Occlusion causes lacunar infarcts.
Appearing darker than surrounding tissue on CT because it absorbs fewer x-rays, as in ischemic stroke or edema.
Relating to examination of the back of the eye (retina, optic disc and vessels) with an ophthalmoscope, used to see hypertensive and diabetic retinopathy.
A non-ergot dopamine agonist used for Parkinson disease and restless legs syndrome.
The light chain that pairs with the heavy chain of MHC class I molecules. Raised in myeloma and a marker of disease burden.
Bacterial enzymes that hydrolyze the beta-lactam ring of penicillins and cephalosporins, causing resistance. Inhibitors include clavulanate.
The fleshy muscle bulge on the little finger side of the palm, supplied by the ulnar nerve. Wasting occurs in ulnar nerve injury.
A recombinant urate oxidase that converts uric acid to soluble allantoin, used to prevent tumor lysis syndrome. Contraindicated in G6PD deficiency.
Transfer of an ADP-ribose group onto a protein. Diphtheria toxin does this to elongation factor 2, halting protein synthesis.
Relating to the greater or lesser trochanter, the bony prominences at the top of the femur. Trochanteric bursitis causes lateral hip pain.
Relating to the endocervix, the canal of the cervix lined by columnar glandular cells. Presence of endocervical cells on Pap smear indicates adequate sampling.
A drug that causes the uterus to contract, such as oxytocin, methylergonovine, carboprost and misoprostol; used to treat postpartum hemorrhage.
Located around the nucleus. Koilocytes have a perinuclear halo in HPV infection, and p-ANCA shows perinuclear staining.
An anion that competitively blocks the sodium-iodide symporter of the thyroid, like perchlorate, reducing iodine uptake. Also a cyanide detoxification product.
